text: The optical energy per multiply-accumulate in an N x N mesh amortizes as 1/N, yet the 'converter wall' still dominates large problems. Why?
choices: The DAC/ADC, laser, and calibration costs are paid once per input/output and do not amortize with N
The optical propagation loss grows as N squared
Lasers become dramatically less efficient as N grows
The Landauer floor rises with matrix size
explanation: A single pass through the mesh performs N-squared products, so the optical energy per MAC falls as 1/N, but the DAC and ADC per data element, the laser power, and the calibration overhead are paid once per input or output and do not amortize, so past a modest size the converters dominate. Optical loss does not scale as N-squared, laser efficiency is not N-dependent, and the Landauer floor is fixed.
